Name: Stephanie Beadle
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I realized this strategy is more helpful than the one I've employed in the past. I've always taught quote sandwiches or ICE (introduce, cite, explain) and it hasn't developed as much thought as SMM has. Also using the graphic organizer and taking more time to teach into the strategy were beneficial. I think I tend to rush things and need to slow down and work through smaller steps with students.

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

I'm continuing to use this strategy with my sophomores going into the end of the semester. We are using it on our weekly articles as well as in our reading notebook. I asked them to use say mean matter on two quotes from their independent reading book (inspired by the discussion!) as we work toward our final character analysis at the end of the semester. We will continue to use it on the final project as well as next semester when we start practicing synthesis essays for the EOC. I'm hoping building this strategy in early will just make the process more natural for them as they continue their educational journeys.
